repeated exposure to the organophosphates DFP and disulfoton decreases carbachol-stiulated phosphoinositid hydrolysis in rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of organophosphate (OP) administration on the central nervous system.
the effects of repeated organophosphates exposure on muscarinic receptor function.
the effects of repeated exposure of rats to two organophosphate pesticides, diisoproplyfluorophosphate and disulfoton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of repeated organophosphates are similar to those seen in acute poisoning, but are more pronounced and more long-lasting.
the effect of repeated OP exposure on phosphoinositide turnover is dependent upon the dose and the type of OP.
repeated organophosphorus exposure results in a decreased carbachol-elicited muscarinic receptor activation, which is coupled to the M3 receptor subtype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repeated organophosphorus compound exposure results in decreased muscarinic receptor-mediated phosphoinositide signaling, as well as decreased acetylcholine synthesis.
repeated organophosphates decrease carbachol-stimulation of phosphoinositide turnover in rat hippocampus.
repeated organophosphates result in a functional decrease of M1 and M2 muscarinic receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
repeated exposure to organophosphates can have effects that are not readily predicted by the acute exposure.
organophosphates are not just a problem for the nervous system.
repeated administration of organophosphate pesticides can lead to a functional downregulation of muscarinic receptor-mediated phosphoinositide turnover.
